cases.prompt: We get LazyInitializationException when Jackson serializes Order.getCustomer() in a controller. Fix it.
expectations: Keeps open-in-view false and moves the mapping into a DTO assembled inside the transaction
Offers an entity graph as the alternative when the entity itself is returned
Rejects enabling open-in-view as the fix and explains the connection cost
Requires the response type to stop being the entity

cases.prompt: hibernate.jdbc.batch_size is 100 but our bulk insert still sends one INSERT per row. Why?
expectations: Identifies GenerationType.IDENTITY as the blocker because the generated key must be returned per row
Proposes a sequence-based generator with an explicit allocationSize
Verifies batch flushing actually occurs and checks ordered inserts
Warns that allocationSize introduces gaps on failed transactions

cases.prompt: Should I turn on the Hibernate second-level cache for our Order entity to speed up reads?
expectations: Asks about write rate and staleness tolerance before answering
Defaults to no for a write-heavy transactional entity
Explains that invalidation becomes application work on every write path
Says to fix the query shape or index first and to prove the query is slow before caching

cases.prompt: We get MultipleBagFetchException when joining orders with both lines and payments.
expectations: Explains that two eager List collections cannot be fetched together
Offers Set for one collection or two separate queries as alternatives
Warns that a join fetch with pagination loads the whole collection and pages in memory
Suggests verifying generated SQL contains the database level limit

cases.prompt: A page of 50 customers takes 400 ms. Suspect N+1 but we have no profiler.
expectations: Enables hibernate.generate_statistics and names the counters to read
Uses getQueryExecutionCount and getCollectionFetchCount as the proof
Offers SQL log grouping as a second, local-only proof
Forbids enabling either in production because of overhead and data exposure

cases.prompt: ddl-auto=update is convenient, can we keep it in the production profile to avoid migration files?
expectations: Rejects ddl-auto in any non-disposable environment
States that update mutates a live schema with no review, history, or rollback
Hands schema ownership to the Flyway skill and asks for expand-and-contract
Allows update or create-drop only against an ephemeral test container
